To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(a) the baseline system, which is a simple extension of the system we submitted last year to TREC-2003, performs well, (b) the system which uses word senses as features performs better than the baseline system, (c) the system which combines statistical similarity measures for relevance and novelty performs better than the system which uses the word senses, (d) the system which performs best is the combination of statistical similarity measures and word senses.

(i) the use of a named entity occurrence database and the associated named entity occurrence database is effective for novelty detection, (ii) word sense similarity can be used to improve the novelty detection process and (iii) statistical similarity schemes, when used to measure the relevance and novelty of a query, are effective in both cases.
the baseline system is the most accurate of the three variations; that word sense is a good predictor of novelty, and that the statistical similarity schemes do not improve performance.

the development and application of statistical techniques for the detection of novel information.
